items.stem: How should a Copilot summary of a diff be used in review?

options.text: As a starting point while the reviewer still reads the diff
options.rationale: Correct: a summary aids review but does not replace reading the change.

options.text: As a full replacement for reading the diff
options.rationale: A summary can miss exactly the risky detail that matters.

options.text: As the sole record, with no human reviewer
options.rationale: A human must stay accountable for the review.
A summary is useful context when used alongside the diff.

items.explanation: Correct: a summary aids review but does not replace reading the change.

items.stem: Which TWO checks confirm a generated test is worth keeping? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: meaningful assertions give a test its value.

options.text: It fails when the behaviour is broken
options.rationale: Correct: a test that cannot fail protects nothing.

options.text: It raises coverage with no assertions
options.rationale: Coverage without assertions is false confidence.

options.text: It always passes regardless of the code

items.explanation: Correct: meaningful assertions give a test its value.

items.stem: A generated test raised coverage but asserts nothing meaningful. What should you do?

options.text: Reject or rewrite it to assert real behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: coverage without assertions gives false confidence.

options.text: Keep it because coverage went up
options.rationale: A higher number with no assertions protects nothing.

options.text: Delete all other tests to match its style

options.rationale: Merging a meaningless test adds no quality.

items.explanation: Correct: coverage without assertions gives false confidence.
